plan: With a private value of $35, I want to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. However, I must anticipate other rational bidders. Given the prize range is $0-$20, but my value is $35, I'll bid strategically high to ensure winning while minimizing overpayment. A bid slightly above the expected maximum competitive bid makes sense.

With a private value of $23, I want to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, I should bid strategically. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to protect against overpaying. Other rational bidders will likely do the same. I'll bid close to, but not exactly at, my value to create strategic uncertainty. A bid around $22.5 seems optimal - high enough to likely win, but not risking paying more than my true value.

My private value is $21, which is actually above the maximum possible randomly drawn value of $20. This suggests a strategic approach. Since other bidders will see me as rational, I want to bid strategically. A pure Nash equilibrium would suggest bidding close to my actual value, but not exactly. I'll bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit, anticipating other bidders might also use similar reasoning.
